title: A submodule of a quasi-coherent module contains a largest quasi-coherent submodule, characterised by its universal property
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement asks for a quasi-coherent O_X-submodule G' of a given submodule G of a quasi-coherent F that corepresents the inclusion G -> F, i.e. Hom(H, G') = Hom(H, G) for every quasi-coherent H, and records that G' is the largest such (statement lines 445-455). The proof is a genuine construction rather than a citation: it takes the direct sum of all quasi-coherent submodules contained in G and defines G' as its image in F (proof lines 459-464), which requires knowing that direct sums and images of maps of quasi-coherent sheaves stay quasi-coherent (proof lines 465-468). The universal property is then proved by observing that for any alpha : H -> G the image of H -> G -> F is itself a quasi-coherent submodule of G, hence already a summand of the direct sum, hence contained in G' (proof lines 472-479). This is H2: one construction plus one short factoring argument, with no hypotheses on X beyond the definitions.
